newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rubber maker sets issue price at PLN 16-25.
newsitem.headline: Polish rubber maker sets issue price at PLN 16-25.

text.p: Polish rubber producer Sanockie Zaklady Przemyslu Gumowego Stomil Sanok SA (Stomil Sanok) set the issue price of its 500,000 new shares at between 16 to 25 zlotys per share, according to the firm's issue prospectus.
The firm said the final issue price would be announced on November 1 at the latest and that it wanted to use the funds from the issue to modernise production.
Investors may subscribe for up to 20,000 shares of the company, which seeks the main market listing, in a public offering scheduled from November 4 to November 15.
Stomil Sanok also said it expected its net profit to soar to 15 million zlotys in 1996 and 16.9 million next year, up from eight million zlotys last year.
It saw its sales rising to 147 million zlotys in 1996 and to 185.4 million next year, up from 111.9 million in 1995.
In the first eight months of 1996 Stomil Sanok had a net profit of 10.8 million zlotys on 91-million-zloty sales.
The Securities Commission earlier cleared Stomil Sanok's existing 4.7 million shares and the new ones for public trade.
The company's main shareholders are the Polish-American Enterprise Fund and the Polish Private Equity Fund I and II, which together hold 78.7 percent of the firm.
Employees and management hold the remaining 21.3 percent.
